podcast.title: Beneficiary of Radio Star Maker
podcast.body: City and Colour's career was furthered by the funding available from the new Radio Star Maker program, introduced in 2000. This program, along with Factor, was instrumental in supporting emerging and established Canadian talent. "Soon this cash was instrumental in helping further the careers of metric, broken social scene, Alexis on fire, city and color, and many more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Eclipsing Alexis on Fire
podcast.body: By the time Dallas Green left Alexis on Fire, his solo project, City and Colour, had grown significantly in popularity. It was noted that City and Colour had "eclipsed Alexis on Fire at that point," influencing Green's decision to leave the band to focus on his creative passion for different musical styles. "City and Colour had a clip to Alexis on fire at that point."

xref.title: Name Change to Arkells (Late 2007/Early 2008)
xref.body: The name change from Charlemagne to Arkells occurred under extreme pressure when Dino Lone Records needed a new name in 45 minutes for an EP flyer to be inserted into the City and Colour record. Max Kermann and Mike DeAngeles, who lived on Arkell Street at the time, proposed the name in a last-minute effort, noting its 60s Motown-esque sound. "So then we frantically got on the phone. I was at the library and McMaster, I still remember. And we called everyone, we got to change the name now because we've been sitting on this kind of decision for a long time and we just hadn't got around to it."

xref.title: Amicable Breakup and Solo Growth – "The Best Thing That Could Have Happened to All of Us"
xref.body: Dallas Green left the band to focus on City and Colour due to creative differences. The remaining members attempted to continue without him before acknowledging that the band without Green would not be Alexisonfire, leading to an amicable split. The separation allowed each member to grow independently; when they reunited, they did so on their own terms, prioritizing enjoyment and work-life balance over the demands of constant touring. "The separation allowed all the members to grow individually, and when they reunited, they did so on their own terms."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dallas Green's Departure
xref.body: Dallas Green decided to leave the band not for solo success, but due to creative differences, feeling he could no longer write aggressive music and did not want to force it. He attempted to continue both Alexis on Fire and City and Colour but found he couldn't write aggressive material naturally anymore. The breakup was amicable, and it was acknowledged that he "probably should have left Alexis on Fire four years earlier" as City and Colour had begun to eclipse Alexis on Fire in popularity. "I left the band solely because I had creatively I wanted to do something else."

xref.title: Departure from Alexisonfire – Creative Differences and Focus on City and Colour
xref.body: Dallas Green left Alexisonfire due to creative differences, seeking to devote himself fully to his solo project City and Colour. His departure was handled amicably and ultimately proved beneficial for all parties. "Left Alexisonfire due to creative differences, seeking to focus on City and Colour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Members' Activities During Hiatus
xref.body: During the band's break, Dallas Green focused on City and Colour; George Pettit became a firefighter; Wade McNeil worked as a radio DJ and in other bands; Jordan Hastings played with Billy Talent; and Chris Steele undertook an expedition to the Himalayas. "Dallas Green focused on City and Colour; George Pettit became a firefighter; Wade McNeil worked as a radio DJ."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Lives
xref.body: Following the band's breakup, members pursued different paths: Dallas Green continued with City and Colour, George Pettit became a firefighter, Wade McNeil became a radio DJ, Jordan Hastings became a fill-in drummer for Billy Talent and played in other bands, and Chris Steele was last heard to have gone for a "truck on the Himalayas." "I mean, Dallas Green is off doing a city and color thing. Vocalist George Pettit became a firefighter. Wade McNeil is doing a bunch of stuff, including working as a radio DJ. Drummer Jordan Hastings is filling it with Billy Talbot and playing in some other bands. And I'm not even sure where bass player Chris Steele is."
